notes: The draft correctly includes single-sex families and handles the documented counterexample. However, A2 adds a common male probability, which overall sex balance and within-family independence do not imply. Take two two-child families with male indicators (U,V) and (1-U,1-V), where U,V are independent Bernoulli(1/4). Each family's sexes are independent, and every realization has exactly two men and two women, yet E[B|male]=5/8 and E[B|female]=3/8. Repeat independent blocks for an arbitrarily large population. Thus Theorem 1 proves equality under stronger assumptions, while the claimed conclusion under the stated assumptions fails.
